children.value: The delta of a neuron is the derivative of the loss with respect to its sum. Output deltas come from the loss, hidden deltas from the deltas of the next layer, weighted with the connecting weights. The gradient of a weight is the input it multiplies times the delta of the neuron it feeds.

The small network has one sigmoid output per class and the squared error as its loss. Classification networks are usually built differently, and the reason lies in the backward pass. A classifier must finally name one class, a hard assignment that keeps the largest output. Its accuracy changes only when the winning class flips, so its gradient is zero almost everywhere, and gradient descent receives no signal from it (
). Training therefore uses a soft assignment: a probability for each class that changes smoothly with the weights. The hard decision follows at prediction time, by picking the most probable class.
